utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, we are in open session,, so Mr. Pantelic, you can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I have informed my colleagues from the Prosecution about the documents in question. According to my list here, first document is D2/1 ID and D2/1 ter ID. The title is "Instruction from the Party of Democratic Action to SDA," dated 20 of January, 1993, during the -- well, during the cross-examination of Dr. Donia I submitted that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. The Prosecution, we now have the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm afraid that is not one of the translations that was handed to me by Defence counsel. I do have another SDA document, dated the 20th of September, 1991. And the other document, D2/1 ID, as far as I can see from my pile here, was not disclosed. So we haven't double-checked on it, but I know that with a number of these documents, which are purported to come from the Party of Democratic Action, that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no. The point is, do you have D2/1 ID?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: D2/1 ter ID? You don't have that?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we deal with the next document? You can deal with that later on. Can we deal with the next one?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. My case manager informed me that it was delivered to the Prosecution a while ago. But no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe they will check later.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Next document is D3/1 ID, and also D3/1 ter ID, which is in the file. That is the excerpt from dictionary about the definition of word "Vakuf," from Croatian dictionary of following words published in 1982.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we do have that and we have no objection to its full admission into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have the confirmation that it will retain the same number now as an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now as an exhibit, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That is D3/1 and --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: ID. D3/1 ter as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I have English translation here with me.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, maybe I'm a little bit confused, but on D3/1 ID and D3/1 ter ID, we have already both documents, one B/C/S and the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry. I can explain. That's unofficial translation, which we used at the beginning of our trial proceedings and then according to the ruling of this Trial Chamber we proceeded with the official translation. So that's the reason why you have this unofficial -- you can disregard. Mr. Usher --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the, yes, official translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now I have the Exhibit D4/1 ID, already submitted D4/1 ter ID, this is a cover page of Muslim newspaper published in October 1991, titled, "New walks", Novi vox, and I have English translation of this cover, front page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we do have that document. However, we do have questions about it being entered into evidence, because it was put to the witness, Mr. Robert Donia, Dr. Robert Donia, who simply said that he was not familiar at all with this publication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: If you could see the document, it seems to have absolutely no relevancy whatsoever to do with this case and on the grounds that it doesn't meet any of the criteria of 89(C), we don't see that it should be admitted into evidence. As I said, it wasn't something that the witness was familiar with and there was nothing I could divine from the transcript that could prove it was in any way relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps counsel could deal with that during the Defence case.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I have certain explanation now, Your Honour, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In fact, this document was tendered into evidence with regard to the general context of Bosnia, where supposedly and allegedly Dr. Donia is familiar. So it's a relation between three ethnic communities, and about the rise of the interethnic tensions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: When was it entered into evidence, because you say it was already --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Offered. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. It was offered by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: By the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It was used during cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's correct. In this broader context of Bosnia history. Well, Dr. Donia is supposed to be an expert. So if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, but he did say that he was not familiar with it, as Ms. Reidy says. So if you still want it, you can call a witness who is familiar and who shows the relevance of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I understand. Then we have D5/1 ID, which is the extract from Official Gazette of socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, constitutional amendments, that we have discussed also with Mr. Donia, according to my list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Again we do have that document. We do, however, have a query. The document which has been given to the translation, the whole document, D5/1 does not seem to be part of the -- it seems to consist of two documents, and only one part of it was put to the witness. And we have -- okay. It's up to -- we have no--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But it's the amendments which even the Court can even take judicial notice of except when you have the document in front of you it's much easier to refer to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: We have no particular objection if relevance could be established later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Can we have the numbers confirmed.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. The numbers will remain the same except for the ID, so as to become exhibits. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, please. I have English translations with me. If you don't mind. Then -- can I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we deal with this one first of all?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can proceed, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Then we have Exhibit D8/1 ID. These are translation, official translation in English. Articles 274 and 275 of the constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina, titled, "Cooperation and association of municipalities."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes: The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: We have know objection, and also just to speed things up, I believe the next exhibit we don't have any objection to either. It will be D9/1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have confirmation. D8/1 and D8/1 ter, they will retain the same numbers as exhibits?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And the next [Microphone not activated] the same numbers will apply this time as exhibits.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Any other documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. D9/1 ID. This is part 4, chapter 4, of the constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Article 416, official English translation. Mr. Usher, please, could I have your assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The next one?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next one is the D15/1 ID, document of HVO Croatian operative group eastern Posavina, command of the Croatian army, Slavonski Brod, dated 28th of May 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Does the Prosecution have that one?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm a little bit confused. I have a document which was handed to me as D15/1 and dated from the 28th of May, 1992, which I believe is the date that Mr. Pantelic read out, although it's not currently recorded in the transcript. But my document says it's from the 102nd Odzak Brigade, and mentions nothing about Slavonski Brod or eastern Posavina, so I don't believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It may not be the same document maybe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Although, Ms. Reidy, I'm just looking at the list of exhibits, and D15/1 is listed as document of HVO Croatian operative group eastern Posavina, command of the Croatian army, Slavonski Brod.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, maybe then that's where it's coming from, but the document that I was handed by Defence counsel as what they call Exhibit D15/1 doesn't bear the same --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Title.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: -- title. So that's -- I don't know which document now Mr. Pantelic is moving to have into evidence as 15/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I have here in the list the title which I just read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe the usher can assist. If counsel -- the English translation you have, if you can -- the one you've just given us the title, if the usher can show it to the Prosecution or give them a copy, we can clear this problem. Yes, Ms. Reidy. Is it --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: It appears to be the same document, so maybe the recording of it in the list of Prosecution's is not correct, because at the time we didn't have a full translation. Maybe that's -- I'm speculating now as to why on the exhibit list it is given a different title, if this is the same document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. It's better for you to be sure. We can deal with this at a later stage if you check through the Prosecution's documents and the list of exhibits we've been given from time to time, so that, you know, you are definite as to which document you are discussing at any time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Maybe I can be of assistance, Your Honour. Can I check B/C/S version, which is actually --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: With the Registry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: With the Registry and then we could see if it fits to the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can the usher please assist with ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I see what is the problem here, Your Honour, if I may. The title of this document in the Registry's list here is actually the stamp, the stamp on the document, and all other elements are the same with the official translation. What I will do now, we could -- you can check, of course, if it's necessary. Everything is the same. But on the other hand, the idea of the Defence was to be focused on this stamp. So maybe in the -- or maybe I can leave it for now and then try to obtain official translation of the stamp, which is also very important element of this document. And then I will tender into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Maybe we can --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Maybe it's better, in order not to have two documents -- two translations about one document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. So you'll deal with that at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Now it's D16/1 ter ID. This is the communication section, attachment number 6 of the SDA armed formation in Bosanski Samac. They are sections. Very often we discussed that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So you now have the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have, of this attachment number 6.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we do have that document, and again, just so we speed up, the next exhibit, D17/1, is of a similar nature. Both of those documents, we would object still to their full admission into evidence, because the witnesses with whom they've been discussed know nothing about the documents, there's no element of authentication. It may be when a further witness comes, either from the Prosecution side or Defence, it could be authenticated. Mr. Tihic didn't know anything about these, so our position still is that they remain ID documents until we can have someone who says what they're about or where they came from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Yes. There appears to be a difference in the designation of the document in the lists we have been given, so I think the safer thing is for both parties to check the transcript. Then we can deal with these documents at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You mean the rest of the documents?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: D16/1 ter and 17/1 and ter. Because it seems from the list we've got that they were actually admitted into evidence on 25th of the 10, 01. In the list we have there's no reference to ID, so there seems to be a bit of confusion here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Oh, yes. I agree. It was admitted and just we wait for the official translation. So that's the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. We'll wait until the Prosecution also can check the transcript. We can deal with that later.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. It was admitted, we also believe. Now I have Exhibit D18/1 ter, which is a handmade drawing by the witness Muhamed Bicic, as marked by the witness, position A, B, et cetera. Mr. Usher, please. Or can we hear from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: On that document, if it was drawn by the witness, then we were waiting for the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. And now we have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes, we have it, and the same applies for the next exhibit, 19/1. Again, to speed things up, we have no objection to 18/1 or 19/1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This is D18, and -- if I understood well. And please, Mr. Usher. And This is D19/1, which is also a sketch of Mr. Ibrahim Salkic, of the secondary school gym.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have confirmation that they retain the same numbers as exhibits?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, they will retain the same numbers but now as exhibits. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, the next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The next document is D20/1 ter ID, a letter from SDA party, headquarters Sarajevo, titled "Information of full readiness of connection and following of SDA," dated 20th of September, 1991. Two pages of letters and four pages of additional information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy. Do you have that document?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, we do have that document. And again, this document we'd ask to -- retains ID status. It was put to Mr. Tihic on the 8th of November, 19 - I'm sorry, 2001 - and the witness had never seen it before, had no knowledge of it, and couldn't say anything about the document. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Yes. The Defence can deal with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- in their case.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. And the last one is the document D21/1 ID, announcement -- title is "Announcement. List of domestic traitors."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecution, you have the English translation?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. Yes, we do have that document, and it was put to Mr. Tihic, who was able to comment on it, so we have no objection to its entry into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Can we have confirmation that it will retain the same number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy, you have something to say?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes. Just again, to save everyone trouble, I just looked at the notes I had written on the documents, because I had checked the transcripts, and Her Honour Judge Williams is correct. Those two documents -- other documents of that nature are ter, but 16 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And 17.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes. 16 and 17, which were, I think, the Hunter [phoen] section, the communications at the time were led into evidence, and we can argue as to whether or not they should be given any weight. But they were at the time entered into evidence, and we, of course, stand by that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Okay. So that sorts out 16 and 17. Yes. Any other document, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I have for D16/1 and D17/1, English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, please. And actually, that's the end of my list of the translated documents for now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I wonder -- if it pleases the Court, I have also a couple of documents which are under no objection, as far as I was told by my colleagues from the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's one of the documents which just -- I just received the translation, and it is a document D23/2 ter ID. It is a salary scale for clerks, typists, couriers, delivering summonses and couriers who work on organisation of work in work brigade. Mr. Usher. I believe that there is no objection to this, to the admittance of this document

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: No. I can confirm that. The Prosecution has no objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Usher. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So we have D23/2 now as an exhibit. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The next one.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm waiting for confirmation by the registry if something is wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. Can we have confirmation, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It is D23/2 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. If I may, Your Honours. It might be much better if we clarify the situation right now. This is an English version, so it should be D23/2, without "ter." I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is correct. I apologise. D23/2. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours, there is another seven documents which have already been given -- the official translation has been given to the registry. The Prosecutor does not have any objection to this, and according to the list which I have in front of me, which was provided by the registry, it says that the decision not yet taken as to its admission. It is probably my fault that while I was introducing the evidence, I didn't ask them to be entered into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So I'm using this opportunity to move this Trial Chamber, so if we can -- if I can go through the list, then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: -- ask for this document to be admitted. And I will read and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Prosecution can check.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: -- I will ask Ms. Reidy to confirm that they don't have any objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. If you can go through the whole list, and then she can confirm at once.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. This is document D11/2 and D11/2 ter. Then the second document is D14/2 and D14/2 ter. Then D15/2 and D15/2 ter. Further, D16/2 ter and D16/2. And further, D17/2 and D17/2 ter. Then D18/2 and D18/2 ter. And the last one, D19/2 ter and D19/2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I can confirm. We have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No objection. All right. Can we just confirm that the documents will retain the same numbers but as exhibits?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Any other matters? We'll adjourn the proceedings until tomorrow at 1415 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 10th day of May, 2002, at 2.15 p.m.
